messages.author: 181bcebaf89c73b8
messages.subject: Generated quantities using optimizing
parts:
I have GP model which I'm running with around N=6000 so even using LBFGS things are a little slow. The test set prediction (which is O(N^3)) is done in generated quantities. Are these generated quantities being calculated on every iteration (even though I don't receive them back from optimizing), or just at convergence? 

Thanks!

David. 

--
David A. Knowles,
Stanford University.

Web: http://cs.stanford.edu/~davidknowles/

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Generated quantities using optimizing
parts:
Hi David,

That's a great question; I think they're run on every iteration, but I haven't 1) looked at code or 2) run a simple example to verify.

The generated quantities are almost never going to be the bulk of computation time, unless you've got a while loop inside or you need to take an inverse somewhere. The i/o might make a difference, depending on your interface and whether you have disks that spin.


Daniel

messages.author: f13fe7e880ed6103
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Generated quantities using optimizing
parts:
My guess is David has both a while loop and an inverse! ;) 

David, can you just comment out the generated quantities block and report back whether there are significant time savings? Also, I guess you're using RStan? I think at some point when I had large covariance matrices (in transformed parameters, not generated quantities, but still...) there was indeed significant i/o overhead, even to the point that I could imagine that just one call to the generated quantities block would be slow what with allocating memory for a 6000x6000 matrix and getting that passed from Stan into R...

Seth
